my 1-paragraph summary of https://t.co/jlVNAITDnw by @meditationstuff https://t.co/aj8rfeRrUM
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image displays a quote about meditation and self-improvement, set against a serene background of a body of water. The quote is written in black text and reads:
    
    "Do stuff that seems good (including nothing) as it seems good, recognizing that your sense of goodness is ever-evolving. Let go of doing stuff if that seems good—you may have more stuff you're still doing that you forgot you kept doing, than you realize. Let your practice evolve too, including your interpretation of these instructions and whether or not you're even conceiving of yourself as following them, by paying attention to what seems to work and not work. Nothing is off-limits; it's a giant puzzle. Have fun!"
    
    The background features a gradient of yellow at the top, gradually transitioning to green towards the bottom, with a subtle image of ripples on the surface of the water.
↓

1574468907921903616 [2022-09-26] @RomeoStevens76 💜 16
@Malcolm_Ocean @meditationstuff (slowly enough to notice what you are doing, completely enough to leave little to no residue)

1574471526358945814 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
@RomeoStevens76 @meditationstuff oooooh nice, yes.

on which note I am doing way too many things right now

===

1622735895593099264 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 26 🔁 1
there's a mode I can get in that is very beautiful and I want it in more of my life

where I'm present and taking care of something, such as cleaning a space, and in each moment I'm just doing whatever cares for it best, with full couldness at several scales

===

1622735901918105600 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 6
just now, I was about to put something in the trash by my desk only to realize I hadn't put a new bag in

so I went mid-writing to go get a bag

the nature of this thread meant that (like the cleaning) I can leave the draft open and it affords finishing
↓
1622735903134486528 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 8
like, simply by looking at the state of the thread, I can figure out what to do with it next

well, that's not totally true; if I waited long enough I might get out of touch with what I'm saying here and I'd at minimum need to re-read it in order for further words to flow
↓
1622735904367611905 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
but there's no disruption caused by getting a trashbag or going pee or something

those only risk disruption if while on such a mission I get waylaid into something deeper or longer
↓
1622735905630072832 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
sometimes though we work in ways that have a lot of context sort of splayed out and it's a bit more delicate

@fortelabs wrote about state of mind as a key resource to knowledge work
https://t.co/GUbTrv8ioO
↓
1622735907081322501 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4
there are maybe two different kinds of splayed-out-ness

one is when the splayed out stuff is in the world, eg
- you have your car taken apart
- a dozen books & papers arranged on your desk
- a half-refactored codebase onto which other changes can't be made
↓
1622735908230565888 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
the other is when your mind is what's splayed out, eg:
- writing a long essay, paper or book, where all the parts are in the world but the WHOLE is in your head
- doing strategy, where you're considering lots of agents, causes, trajectories 
- this ofc:
https://t.co/cKjtUNxeVm
  [Quoting Tweet 843947482769907712 (missing)]
↓
1622735909732110336 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
there's also something like arc momentum

I was recently organizing expenses for taxes, and each action locally took only 1 min and was very obvious in next steps

so I was locally quite interruptible

but when a short walk turned into a (lovely!) long walk, something was lost
↓
1622735910982017024 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
I suppose that part of what was lost was actually mental context—my spreadsheet was tracking a bunch of stuff, but it wasn't remembering every place I'd looked or sorting decision I'd made

so finishing the task a later day risked some duplication of effort
↓
1622735912038977537 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
there's also something about the satisfaction of completing something in one day / arc

I suspect this is partially about open loops, like I wanted to finish it because I didn't want it to remain open and I didn't know how to close it without finishing it
↓
1622735913242738689 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4
most people are not very good at feeling the simple moment of satisfaction & vast micro-rest when completing something (even a tiny fraction of some larger something)
https://t.co/tBFlN4Nbdm
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: nothing-to-do meditation aka "allow myself to die in this moment"  I've been experimenting with this a bit over the last few years, and moreso the last week, and finding it quite potent. idk what the deal is exactly but here are some thoughts]
↓
1622735914589102080 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
this tweet by @RomeoStevens76 has been a really useful set of simple instructions for getting into this mode of being for me

https://t.co/PDOp9ZJr8h
  [Quoting @RomeoStevens76: @Malcolm_Ocean @meditationstuff Do one thing at a time Do it slowly, and completely Between things, pause Sometimes make the thing you are doing nothing]
↓
1622735916593991681 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
all of this feels related to the Complice "Now Page" which is a page that shows you just your current intention (or some dropdowns/inputs for choosing an intention)

and to which I recently added an animation
https://t.co/YXpjSdmK4P
  [Quoting Tweet 1622729274729062400 (missing)]
↓
1622735918154289152 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
another lil case study: I wanted to show you the animation, not to just talk about it, but this required a multi-step task that was sort of "outside" of writing this thread:
- ship the code (took 20s; it was ready in test mode)
- screen capture
- make gif
- tweet
↓
1622735919379025920 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
if I'd gotten interrupted in the middle of that task, it could have felt quite stressful; this is in part because the twitter thread composer doesn't save drafts so it's scary to leave something open for awhile to return to

but also in part because it's sort of just a tall stack
↓
1622735920607920128 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
this might be a good reminder that sometimes I tweet better when I'm sending one tweet at a time rather than composing the whole thread at once

on which note, gonna hit send now even tho more to say
https://t.co/IqMEcwZNDo
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: I wanna try shooting from the hip]
↓
1622736261818781696 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
okay where was I? I was sort of orienting towards today as a writing day, and part of what was on my mind when I started writing this thread (a couple hours ago now given the little things that have made their way into the cracks)

…how do I access this fluid mode while writing?
↓
1622742335846252544 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
I suppose in some sense writing one tweet at a time has a bit of this fluid small-deliverable couldness quality (editing is a whole nother workflow mystery)

paradoxically, I got distracted after writing the first half of that tweet, and found this:
https://t.co/Uq3IOfz2pw
  [Quoting Tweet 1622316768785047558 (missing)]
↓
1622742801967640576 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
there's definitely something about the unshippedness of things that motivates me to finish writing them though, and I don't think that's a confusion

when I was working on my 20k word "How We Get There" last year, wanting to share it w friends was the main driver of finishing it
↓
1622744012875780096 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
like I was saying at the top—it had no checkbox

it had a desired world state which was "my friends are reading it" and I wanted it to be done before they did, so every time I wanted them to read it, I WANTED to finish writing it
https://t.co/eNA1KLDlGm
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: you are absolutely free to do what you want  you are not free from the consequences of doing what you do  you wouldn't want to be—otherwise what would be the point of doing it?]
↓
1622744195340599296 [2023-02-06] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
I'm recognizing that despite my overall goal-orientedness and understanding of PCT (which has this perception-desire-gap model of motivation)

...I still do a lot of stuff with push energy rather than pull energy.
↓
1622746997785763840 [2023-02-07] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
it's harder to focus when I have a lot of open tabs. often those tabs are representing nebulous unconscious half-intentions, but then they turn into stale clutter that I'm pulled towards clearing away—but clearing isn't WHY to read this article!!

https://t.co/9YiUEYACvR
